limitations: The fixture declares approved capability owners but does not prove that an implementation actually imported one.
Library comparison and performance require source and runtime evidence beyond screenshots.

brief.productIntent: Help a QA engineer explore a dense project relationship graph while preserving an accessible equivalent list for the same nodes and edges.
userJobs: Filter graph nodes by business-object type
Focus one node and inspect its neighborhood
Reach the same relationships through a keyboard-accessible list fallback
contentTruth: The graph contains processes, roles, rules, entities, and Automated checks
Sample approval flow connects to two roles, three rules, and one Automated check
The list fallback represents the same focused neighborhood

typographyRoles: Compact UI sans-serif for filters and inspector controls
Readable neutral labels inside graph nodes and fallback rows
colorRoles: Object types use a restrained categorical palette
Selection uses cobalt without glow-heavy decoration
spacingAndShape: Dense canvas balanced by a stable inspector rail
Compact low-radius controls and clear focus rings
componentPosture: Analytical and inspectable rather than ornamental
Fallback is a first-class equivalent view, not a hidden accessibility afterthought
imageryRole: No decorative imagery; nodes and edges carry the visual content
motionTone: Short focus and pan transitions with reduced-motion compatibility

capabilityFit.capability: Interactive force-directed relationship exploration with an equivalent accessible list
capabilityFit.customPrimitiveAllowedWhen: Only when documented project evidence shows every established owner fails a required graph behavior or constraint.

avoid: A bespoke glowing canvas with no inspector discipline
A custom interaction vocabulary inconsistent with the product
